```renyi
module savings.schedule
  purpose: Print a yearly compound-interest savings schedule.

import std.console
import std.environment

type AppError is one of
  UsageError(detail: Text)
  BadStartingAmount(input: Text)
  BadRate(input: Text)
  BadYears(input: Text)
end

function usage_text()
  returns Text
  purpose: Describe the command-line arguments.
  example: usage_text() is "usage: savings <starting_amount> <yearly_rate_percent> <years>"

  return "usage: savings <starting_amount> <yearly_rate_percent> <years>"
end

function round_to_cents(amount: Decimal)
  returns Decimal
  purpose: Round a decimal amount to the nearest cent.
  example: round_to_cents(12.346) is 12.35

  let cents be (amount * 100.00).rounded()
  return cents.to_decimal() / 100.00
end

function balance_after_year(balance: Decimal, yearly_rate_percent: Decimal)
  returns Decimal
  purpose: Compute the next yearly balance after applying compound interest.
  example: balance_after_year(balance: 100.00, yearly_rate_percent: 5.00) is 105.00

  let growth_factor be 1.00 + yearly_rate_percent / 100.00
  let unrounded_balance be balance * growth_factor
  return round_to_cents(unrounded_balance)
end

function money_text(amount: Decimal)
  returns Text
  purpose: Format a decimal amount with exactly two digits after the decimal point.
  example: money_text(105.5) is "105.50"

  let rounded_amount be round_to_cents(amount)
  let amount_text be rounded_amount.to_text()
  let parts be amount_text.split(".")
  if parts.length() is 1 then
    return "{amount_text}.00"
  otherwise
    let whole_part be parts.at(0) otherwise crash with "decimal text without whole part"
    let fractional_part be parts.at(1) otherwise crash with "decimal text without fractional part"
    if fractional_part.length() is 0 then
      return "{whole_part}.00"
    otherwise if fractional_part.length() is 1 then
      return "{whole_part}.{fractional_part}0"
    otherwise
      return "{whole_part}.{fractional_part.take(2)}"
    end
  end
end

function schedule_line(year: Integer, balance: Decimal)
  returns Text
  purpose: Build one printable line of the savings schedule.
  example: schedule_line(year: 2, balance: 110.2) is "Year 2: 110.20"

  return "Year {year}: {money_text(balance)}"
end

public function main()
  or fails with AppError
  needs console, environment
  purpose: Print a yearly savings balance schedule from command-line arguments.

  let arguments be environment.arguments()
  if arguments.length() is not 3 then
    fail with UsageError(detail: usage_text())
  end

  let amount_text be arguments.at(0) otherwise fail with UsageError(detail: usage_text())
  let rate_text be arguments.at(1) otherwise fail with UsageError(detail: usage_text())
  let years_text be arguments.at(2) otherwise fail with UsageError(detail: usage_text())

  let starting_amount be amount_text.to_decimal() otherwise fail with BadStartingAmount(input: amount_text)
  let yearly_rate_percent be rate_text.to_decimal() otherwise fail with BadRate(input: rate_text)
  let years be years_text.to_integer() otherwise fail with BadYears(input: years_text)

  if starting_amount is less than 0.00 then
    fail with BadStartingAmount(input: amount_text)
  end

  if yearly_rate_percent is less than 0.00 then
    fail with BadRate(input: rate_text)
  end

  if years is less than 0 then
    fail with BadYears(input: years_text)
  end

  console.print("Year Balance")

  let mutable year be 0
  let mutable balance be round_to_cents(starting_amount)
  console.print(schedule_line(year: year, balance: balance))

  repeat until year is at least years
    set year to year + 1
    set balance to balance_after_year(balance: balance, yearly_rate_percent: yearly_rate_percent)
    console.print(schedule_line(year: year, balance: balance))
  end
end
```

```renyi
module savings.schedule
  purpose: Print a yearly savings balance schedule with compound interest.

import std.console
import std.environment

public type InputError is one of
  purpose: A command-line value that cannot be used for the savings schedule.
  WrongArgumentCount(actual: Integer)
  BadAmount(value: Text)
  BadRate(value: Text)
  BadYears(value: Text)
end

public function main()
  or fails with InputError
  needs console, environment
  purpose: Print the yearly savings balance schedule from command-line arguments.

  let args be environment.arguments()
  let argument_count be args.length()

  if argument_count is not 3 then
    console.print_error("Usage: savings.schedule <starting amount> <yearly rate percent> <years>")
    fail with WrongArgumentCount(actual: argument_count)
  otherwise
    let amount_text be args.at(0) otherwise crash with "argument count was checked"
    let rate_text be args.at(1) otherwise crash with "argument count was checked"
    let years_text be args.at(2) otherwise crash with "argument count was checked"

    let starting_balance be parse_amount(amount_text) otherwise fail
    let yearly_rate_percent be parse_rate(rate_text) otherwise fail
    let years be parse_years(years_text) otherwise fail

    console.print("Year  Balance")

    let mutable year be 0
    let mutable balance be starting_balance
    let opening_balance_text be format_money(balance)
    console.print("{year}     {opening_balance_text}")

    repeat until year is at least years
      set year to year + 1
      set balance to balance_after_year(balance: balance, yearly_rate_percent: yearly_rate_percent)
      let current_balance_text be format_money(balance)
      console.print("{year}     {current_balance_text}")
    end
  end
end

function parse_amount(text: Text)
  returns Decimal
  or fails with InputError
  purpose: Read a non-negative starting amount and round it to cents.
  example: parse_amount("12.34") is 12.34

  let cleaned be text.trim()
  let amount be cleaned.to_decimal() otherwise fail with BadAmount(value: text)

  if amount is less than 0.00 then
    fail with BadAmount(value: text)
  otherwise
    return round_to_cents(amount)
  end
end

function parse_rate(text: Text)
  returns Decimal
  or fails with InputError
  purpose: Read a non-negative yearly interest rate in percent.
  example: parse_rate("5.5") is 5.5

  let cleaned be text.trim()
  let rate be cleaned.to_decimal() otherwise fail with BadRate(value: text)

  if rate is less than 0.00 then
    fail with BadRate(value: text)
  otherwise
    return rate
  end
end

function parse_years(text: Text)
  returns Integer
  or fails with InputError
  purpose: Read a non-negative number of whole years.
  example: parse_years("3") is 3

  let cleaned be text.trim()
  let years be cleaned.to_integer() otherwise fail with BadYears(value: text)

  if years is less than 0 then
    fail with BadYears(value: text)
  otherwise
    return years
  end
end

function cents_from_decimal(amount: Decimal)
  returns Integer
  purpose: Convert a decimal money amount to rounded cents.
  example: cents_from_decimal(12.34) is 1234

  let cents be (amount * 100.00).rounded()
  return cents
end

function round_to_cents(amount: Decimal)
  returns Decimal
  purpose: Round a decimal money amount to the nearest cent.
  example: round_to_cents(12.34) is 12.34

  let cents be cents_from_decimal(amount)
  return cents.to_decimal() / 100.00
end

function balance_after_year(balance: Decimal, yearly_rate_percent: Decimal)
  returns Decimal
  purpose: Apply one year of compound interest and round the result to cents.
  example: balance_after_year(balance: 100.00, yearly_rate_percent: 5.00) is 105.00

  let multiplier be (100.00 + yearly_rate_percent) / 100.00
  return round_to_cents(balance * multiplier)
end

function format_money(amount: Decimal)
  returns Text
  purpose: Format a decimal money amount with exactly two digits of cents.
  example: format_money(12.30) is "12.30"

  let cents be cents_from_decimal(amount)
  let dollars be cents.quotient(100)
  let pennies be cents remainder 100
  let pennies_text be if pennies is less than 10 then "0{pennies}" otherwise pennies.to_text() end
  return "{dollars}.{pennies_text}"
end
```

```renyi
module savings.schedule
  purpose: Print a yearly compound-interest savings schedule.

import std.console
import std.environment

type AppError is one of
  purpose: A command-line input error for the savings schedule.
  Usage(message: Text)
  BadAmount(value: Text)
  BadRate(value: Text)
  BadYears(value: Text)
end

type ScheduleInput
  purpose: Values needed to compute a savings schedule.
  has starting_amount: Decimal
  has rate_percent: Decimal
  has years: Integer
end

public function main()
  needs environment, console
  purpose: Read command-line arguments and print a compound-interest savings schedule.

  let command_arguments be environment.arguments()
  match parse_arguments(command_arguments)
    when success(input) then print_schedule(input)
    when failure(error) then console.print_error(error_message(error))
  end
end

function parse_arguments(command_arguments: List of Text)
  returns ScheduleInput
  or fails with AppError
  purpose: Parse the starting amount, yearly rate percent and number of years.
  example: parse_arguments(["100.00", "5.00", "2"]) is ScheduleInput(starting_amount: 100.00, rate_percent: 5.00, years: 2)

  if command_arguments.length() is not 3 then
    fail with Usage(message: usage_text())
  end

  let starting_text be command_arguments.at(0) otherwise fail with Usage(message: usage_text())
  let rate_text be command_arguments.at(1) otherwise fail with Usage(message: usage_text())
  let years_text be command_arguments.at(2) otherwise fail with Usage(message: usage_text())

  let amount be starting_text.to_decimal() otherwise fail with BadAmount(value: starting_text)
  if amount is less than 0.00 then
    fail with BadAmount(value: starting_text)
  end

  let rate be rate_text.to_decimal() otherwise fail with BadRate(value: rate_text)
  if rate is less than 0.00 then
    fail with BadRate(value: rate_text)
  end

  let years be years_text.to_integer() otherwise fail with BadYears(value: years_text)
  if years is less than 0 then
    fail with BadYears(value: years_text)
  end

  return ScheduleInput(starting_amount: round_to_cent(amount), rate_percent: rate, years: years)
end

function usage_text()
  returns Text
  purpose: Give the expected command-line syntax.
  example: usage_text() is "usage: savings_schedule START_AMOUNT YEARLY_RATE_PERCENT YEARS"

  return "usage: savings_schedule START_AMOUNT YEARLY_RATE_PERCENT YEARS"
end

function error_message(error: AppError)
  returns Text
  purpose: Convert a command-line input error into a message.
  example: error_message(Usage(message: "bad input")) is "bad input"

  match error
    when Usage(message) then return message
    when BadAmount(value) then return "starting amount must be a non-negative decimal amount: {value}; {usage_text()}"
    when BadRate(value) then return "yearly rate percent must be a non-negative decimal number: {value}; {usage_text()}"
    when BadYears(value) then return "years must be a non-negative integer: {value}; {usage_text()}"
  end
end

function round_to_cent(amount: Decimal)
  returns Decimal
  purpose: Round a decimal amount to the nearest cent.
  example: round_to_cent(10.001) is 10.00

  let cents be amount * 100.00
  let rounded_cents be cents.rounded()
  return rounded_cents.to_decimal() / 100.00
end

function next_balance(balance: Decimal, rate_percent: Decimal)
  returns Decimal
  purpose: Apply one year of compound interest and round the result to the cent.
  example: next_balance(balance: 100.00, rate_percent: 5.00) is 105.00

  let interest be balance * rate_percent / 100.00
  let unrounded_balance be balance + interest
  return round_to_cent(unrounded_balance)
end

function format_cent_amount(amount: Decimal)
  returns Text
  purpose: Format a cent-rounded amount with two fractional digits.
  example: format_cent_amount(10.00) is "10.00"

  let amount_text be amount.to_text()
  let parts be amount_text.split(".")
  let whole be parts.at(0) otherwise return amount_text

  if parts.length() is 1 then
    return "{whole}.00"
  end

  let cents_text be parts.at(1) otherwise return "{whole}.00"

  if cents_text.length() is 0 then
    return "{whole}.00"
  end

  if cents_text.length() is 1 then
    return "{whole}.{cents_text}0"
  end

  let shown_cents be cents_text.take(2)
  return "{whole}.{shown_cents}"
end

function print_schedule(input: ScheduleInput)
  needs console
  purpose: Print the starting balance and each yearly compound-interest balance.

  let mutable balance be input.starting_amount
  let starting_text be format_cent_amount(balance)
  console.print("Year 0: {starting_text}")

  if input.years is greater than 0 then
    for each year in from 1 to input.years
      set balance to next_balance(balance: balance, rate_percent: input.rate_percent)
      let balance_text be format_cent_amount(balance)
      console.print("Year {year}: {balance_text}")
    end
  end
end
```

```renyi
public type AppError is one of

  purpose: Describe the required command-line arguments.

function round_to_cents(amount: Decimal)
  returns Decimal
  purpose: Round a decimal amount to the nearest cent.

  let rounded_scaled be scaled.rounded()
  return rounded_scaled / 100.00

function format_money(amount: Decimal)
  returns Text
  purpose: Format a decimal amount with exactly two digits after the decimal point.
  example: format_money(12.3) is "12.30"

  let rounded_amount be round_to_cents(amount)

    let whole be parts.at(0) otherwise crash with "decimal text has no whole part"

      return "{whole}.{cents}0"

    if cents.length() is 2 then
      return text
    end

    let two_cents be cents.take(2)
    return "{whole}.{two_cents}"
  otherwise
    return "{text}.00"
  end
end

  returns Decimal
  purpose: Apply one year of compound interest and round the balance to cents.

  let rate be text.to_decimal() otherwise fail with InvalidArgument(message: "Yearly rate percent must be a decimal number.")

  if rate is less than 0.00 then
    fail with InvalidArgument(message: "Yearly rate percent must not be negative.")
  end

  return rate
end

function parse_years(text: Text)
  returns Integer
  or fails with AppError
  purpose: Parse and validate the number of years.
  example: parse_years("3") is 3

  let years be text.to_integer() otherwise fail with InvalidArgument(message: "Years must be an integer.")

  if years is less than 0 then
    fail with InvalidArgument(message: "Years must not be negative.")
  end

  return years
end

function read_request(args: List of Text)
  returns SavingsRequest
  or fails with AppError
  purpose: Parse all command-line arguments into a savings schedule request.
  example: read_request(["1000.00", "5.00", "2"]) is SavingsRequest(starting_amount: 1000.00, yearly_rate_percent: 5.00, years: 2)

  if args.length() is not 3 then

  let rate_text be args.at(1) otherwise fail with Usage(message: usage_text())

  let yearly_rate_percent be parse_yearly_rate_percent(rate_text) otherwise fail
  let years be parse_years(years_text) otherwise fail

  return SavingsRequest(starting_amount: starting_amount, yearly_rate_percent: yearly_rate_percent, years: years)

    for each year in from 1 to request.years
      set balance to balance_after_year(balance: balance, yearly_rate_percent: request.yearly_rate_percent)
      console.print(schedule_line(year: year, balance: balance))
    end
  end

public function main() or fails with AppError
  needs console, environment
  purpose: Print a yearly savings balance schedule from command-line arguments.

  let args be environment.arguments()
  let request be read_request(args) otherwise fail
  print_schedule(request)
```

```renyi
module savings.schedule
  purpose: Print a yearly compound-interest savings schedule.

import std.console
import std.environment

type CommandLine
  purpose: The validated command-line values for the savings schedule.
  has starting_balance: Decimal
  has yearly_rate_percent: Decimal
  has years: Integer
end

type ScheduleLine
  purpose: One displayed balance at the end of a year.
  has year: Integer
  has balance: Decimal
end

type AppError is one of
  purpose: A problem with the command-line input.
  Usage(message: Text)
  BadArgument(name: Text, value: Text, reason: Text)
end

public function main()
  needs console, environment
  purpose: Print a yearly compound-interest savings schedule.

  let arguments be environment.arguments()
  match parse_arguments(arguments)
    when success(command) then
      let schedule be build_schedule(command)
      print_schedule(schedule)
    when failure(error) then
      console.print_error(error_message(error))
  end
end

function parse_arguments(arguments: List of Text)
  returns CommandLine
  or fails with AppError
  purpose: Convert the command-line arguments into schedule inputs.
  example: parse_arguments(["100.00", "5.00", "2"]) is CommandLine(starting_balance: 100.00, yearly_rate_percent: 5.00, years: 2)

  if arguments.length() is not 3 then
    fail with Usage(message: "Usage: savings START_AMOUNT YEARLY_RATE_PERCENT YEARS")
  end

  let starting_text be arguments.at(0) otherwise fail with Usage(message: "Usage: savings START_AMOUNT YEARLY_RATE_PERCENT YEARS")
  let rate_text be arguments.at(1) otherwise fail with Usage(message: "Usage: savings START_AMOUNT YEARLY_RATE_PERCENT YEARS")
  let years_text be arguments.at(2) otherwise fail with Usage(message: "Usage: savings START_AMOUNT YEARLY_RATE_PERCENT YEARS")

  let starting_balance be parse_decimal_argument(name: "starting amount", value: starting_text) otherwise fail
  let yearly_rate_percent be parse_decimal_argument(name: "yearly rate percent", value: rate_text) otherwise fail
  let years be parse_years_argument(years_text) otherwise fail

  return CommandLine(starting_balance: starting_balance, yearly_rate_percent: yearly_rate_percent, years: years)
end

function parse_decimal_argument(name: Text, value: Text)
  returns Decimal
  or fails with AppError
  purpose: Parse a non-negative decimal command-line argument.
  example: parse_decimal_argument(name: "starting amount", value: "12.34") is 12.34

  let parsed be value.to_decimal() otherwise fail with BadArgument(name: name, value: value, reason: "must be a decimal number")
  if parsed is less than 0.00 then
    fail with BadArgument(name: name, value: value, reason: "must not be negative")
  end

  return parsed
end

function parse_years_argument(value: Text)
  returns Integer
  or fails with AppError
  purpose: Parse a positive whole number of years.
  example: parse_years_argument("3") is 3

  let parsed be value.to_integer() otherwise fail with BadArgument(name: "years", value: value, reason: "must be a whole number")
  if parsed is less than 1 then
    fail with BadArgument(name: "years", value: value, reason: "must be at least 1")
  end

  return parsed
end

function build_schedule(command: CommandLine)
  returns List of ScheduleLine
  purpose: Build the starting balance and each compounded yearly balance.
  example: build_schedule(CommandLine(starting_balance: 100.00, yearly_rate_percent: 10.00, years: 2)) is [ScheduleLine(year: 0, balance: 100.00), ScheduleLine(year: 1, balance: 110.00), ScheduleLine(year: 2, balance: 121.00)]

  let starting_balance be round_to_cent(command.starting_balance)
  let yearly_factor be 1.00 + command.yearly_rate_percent / 100.00
  let mutable balance be starting_balance
  let mutable schedule: List of ScheduleLine be [ScheduleLine(year: 0, balance: starting_balance)]

  for each year in from 1 to command.years
    set balance to round_to_cent(balance * yearly_factor)
    set schedule to schedule.append(ScheduleLine(year: year, balance: balance))
  end

  return schedule
end

function round_to_cent(amount: Decimal)
  returns Decimal
  purpose: Round a decimal amount to the nearest cent.
  example: round_to_cent(12.344) is 12.34

  let cents be (amount * 100.00).rounded()
  return cents / 100.00
end

function print_schedule(schedule: List of ScheduleLine)
  needs console
  purpose: Print the schedule table.

  console.print("Year | Balance")
  console.print("-----|--------")

  for each line in schedule
    console.print(format_schedule_line(line))
  end
end

function format_schedule_line(line: ScheduleLine)
  returns Text
  purpose: Format one schedule row for display.
  example: format_schedule_line(ScheduleLine(year: 1, balance: 105.00)) is "1 | 105.00"

  let balance_text be format_money(line.balance)
  return "{line.year} | {balance_text}"
end

function format_money(amount: Decimal)
  returns Text
  purpose: Format a decimal amount with exactly two cent digits.
  example: format_money(105.00) is "105.00"

  let rounded_amount be round_to_cent(amount)
  let rounded_text be rounded_amount.to_text()

  if not rounded_text.contains(".") then
    return "{rounded_text}.00"
  end

  let pieces be rounded_text.split(".")
  let whole be pieces.at(0) otherwise crash with "decimal text has no whole part"
  let fraction be pieces.at(1) otherwise crash with "decimal text has no fraction part"

  if fraction.length() is 0 then
    return "{whole}.00"
  otherwise if fraction.length() is 1 then
    return "{whole}.{fraction}0"
  otherwise
    let cents be fraction.take(2)
    return "{whole}.{cents}"
  end
end

function error_message(error: AppError)
  returns Text
  purpose: Convert an input error into a message for the user.
  example: error_message(Usage(message: "bad input")) is "bad input"

  match error
    when Usage(message) then return message
    when BadArgument(name, value, reason) then return "{name} '{value}' is invalid: {reason}"
  end
end
```
